name: PwrQ
old_description: Same products. Same solutions. Now backed by the speed of Forgent.
about:
PwrQ is based in Hanover, Maryland, and traces its roots to 1926. The company is now part of Forgent, a platform that brings together over a century of experience in power infrastructure. No founder names are disclosed, and ownership details beyond the Forgent affiliation are not specified.

PwrQ designs and manufactures low-voltage power distribution equipment, including its S1 switchboard line, remote power panels (RPP), panelboards (120/208 V to 600 V), and power distribution units (PDU) with integrated monitoring. The company operates vertically integrated facilities that handle raw copper busbar fabrication, CNC turret punching, laser cutting, robotic welding, and final assembly and test. Dedicated production lanes for each product family enable high-volume, high-precision output. A planned 220,000-square-foot expansion near the current headquarters will add capacity.

The company serves hyperscale data centers, manufacturing plants, utility and grid operators, hospitals, and other mission-critical facilities. Its engineering teams support projects from utility service entrance to rack-level load, while field service crews provide preventive maintenance, commissioning, retrofits, and generator solutions (3 kW to 10 MW) across the U.S.

PwrQ emphasizes that vertical integration gives it control over quality, lead times, and capacity. Dedicated lanes and AI-driven machinery aim to reduce variability and accelerate throughput. The firm also highlights its end-to-end engineering capability—spanning single-line design, selective coordination, arc-flash studies, and SCADA/BMS integration—as a differentiator for complex, fast-paced projects.
